# 67js

> 3D engine that AI agents drive. Real-time WebGL2 scenes in the browser and deterministic PNG/MP4 output from the same scene.

This file is a compact map for LLMs and coding agents. The linked guide contains the API contract and runnable examples.
Unreleased changes, with issue numbers and breaking flags, are in changelog.json next to release.json on the site. Check it before you rely on a feature from the docs.
The installed package determines available APIs. Release metadata describes the website's release, which can differ from a local checkout.

## Read only what your task needs

Version `0.5.0` adds `67js/addons/agent-scene` and the `67js-mcp` command.
Version `0.6.0` adds asynchronous snapshot render jobs. Read `/agent-render-jobs.md` for submission, progress, cancellation and artifact results.

Version `0.8.0` adds imported source-node overrides and motion. Read `/agent-character-motion.md` for joint IDs, layering and pose ownership.

Variants: `scene_apply` with a `branch` name forks without editing, `scene_review` shots take a `branch`, `scene_restore` with `branch` keeps one; `labels: true` on `scene_look` and `scene_review` prints and returns part names and lint with pixel positions.
Version `0.9.0` adds `scene_review`. Read `/agent-review.md` for a labeled PNG grid of up to four views or poses.
Review uses an isolated snapshot with separate camera and clock settings. It preserves the source revision and preview pose.

Version `0.7.0` adds recipe motion and atomic set-motion authoring. Read `/agent-motion.md` before generating tracks.
Use scene_look motionTime for absolute procedural preview seeks. Omit it to preserve the last pose, or use null for the authored base.

Preview seeks do not advance revisions. Creation, edits and restore sample zero when motion exists.
Jobs use settings.motion.start plus elapsed time. Imported clips and renderer shader time retain separate controls.

Read `/agent-scene.md` for versioned JSON recipes, stable IDs, expected revisions, atomic edits and bounded checkpoints.
Use `session.inspect()` for compact object facts and `session.exportRecipe()` for detached JSON.
Keep renderer-facing geometry immutable. Call `renderer.updateParts(session.parts)` after a successful edit or restore.
This addon does not expose an MCP server or a render job queue.

The npm package includes a prebuilt stdio MCP server. After alias installation, run `npx 67js-mcp --backend gpu --memory 192` with Node.js 20.19+ and installed Chrome.
Install with `npm install 67js@npm:@codepawlhq/67js` so imports stay `67js`. A plain `npm install @codepawlhq/67js` puts the package in `node_modules/@codepawlhq/67js` instead.
For MCP clients, invoke Node directly with the absolute path to `node_modules/67js/bin/67js-mcp.mjs`. Read `/mcp.md` for configuration.
The browser starts only when creating a scene. No source checkout, Vite build or browser download is required.

Read `/mcp.md` before configuring it. Start with `scene_capabilities`, create a recipe and inspect its stable IDs.

Read `/agent-asset.md` for imported asset sessions available since `0.5.0` and the `67js/addons/agent-asset` addon.
Configure --assets with an absolute GLB directory, then call scene_asset_catalog and scene_create_asset with a content-bound asset ID.
Imported scenes preserve supported maps, skins, morphs and clips. Their topology remains fixed.

Use scene_inspect kind:hierarchy with offset/limit to find source node-N IDs and editable joints. Mesh-N IDs describe primitives.
Use set-asset-node for local TRS and set-motion for source-node, material and camera tracks. Preserve the decoded rig and textures.
Use set-root for asset placement and set-animation for absolute clip/time sampling. Checkpoint before sampling or relighting.

Read `/agent-look.md` for recipe environment, effects and shadow fields.
Use `set-environment`, `set-effects` and `set-shadow` for atomic partial look patches.
Nested volumeFog/bloom fields merge. pointLights replaces the list. Volume fog requires HDR/depth support.

Checkpoint before relighting, inspect the PNG, then restore or export the full recipe. Point lights do not cast local shadows.

Checkpoint, apply small revisioned batches, then use `scene_look` to assess the actual PNG.
Restore failed experiments and release unused checkpoints. Export the recipe and dispose the scene when finished.
The runtime keeps one browser scene alive, serializes calls, caps PNG responses and releases resources on stdin EOF.

Use `add-geometry`, `add-material` and `add-node` records to build a scene from an empty recipe.
Use explicit removal commands and `set-node` geometry/material fields to rebind meshes. Final batch references must resolve.
Removing a parent requires `recursive: true` or reparenting/removing its children in the same batch.

Active, checkpoint and staged geometry share a budget. Release unused checkpoints before increasing detail.
Topology changes reconcile rigid, untextured GPU parts. Geometry stays immutable and surviving shared buffers remain allocated.

Tools accept bounded JSON and configured local assets. They expose no arbitrary code, remote asset providers or caller-selected file paths.

- [Release metadata](https://67js.codepawl.com/release.json): package name, version, publication status, install command, module URL and commit.
- [Complete plain-text guide](https://67js.codepawl.com/guide.md): renderer, parts, materials, cameras, animation, lifecycle, export and troubleshooting. The section "Render a PNG from a script without MCP" is a tested script for an agent with no MCP client.
- [GLB contract](https://67js.codepawl.com/gltf.md): supported assets and conversion limits. Read before selecting or importing a model.
- [Documentation](https://67js.codepawl.com/docs.html): the human reading interface for the same guide.

Use guide headings to locate a task. Parts and geometry covers scene construction. Renderer reference covers options and diagnostics.
Images and films covers the repository CLI. Performance and memory covers allocation planning. Models and AI agents covers completion evidence.

## Installation and API discovery

1. Read release metadata before choosing the published version or browser module URL.
2. Install the short import alias with `npm install 67js@npm:@codepawlhq/67js`.
3. Compare the imported `VERSION` with your installed package metadata.
4. Read the matching guide section before generating API calls.

Without the alias, imports use `@codepawlhq/67js`. Aliased core imports use `67js`.
Addon paths include `67js/addons/model`, `67js/addons/nature`, `67js/addons/film`, `67js/addons/motion`, `67js/addons/canvas2d` and `67js/addons/gltf`.
The core exports `Renderer67`, `box`, `cylinder`, `sphere`, `torus`, camera helpers, animation helpers, effects and budget helpers.
Exact signatures and defaults are in the guide. Names from Three.js are not substitutes for 67js APIs.

## Build a scene

1. Define the subject, camera, interaction, output dimensions and memory budget.
2. Create uniquely named parts with shared geometry, materials and finite invertible column-major matrices.
3. Set explicit MSAA, HDR, pixel ratio and `memoryBudgetMiB` options.
4. Reuse one renderer and update existing parts through `updateParts`.
5. Render on demand for static scenes and pause continuous playback when hidden.
6. Provide keyboard controls and honor reduced motion.
7. Disconnect observers, cancel animation frames and dispose owned resources during teardown.

Material RGB values are linear. Repeated meshes share geometry object identity, rather than separate copies with equal values.
`updateParts` changes retained parts. A different graph requires a new renderer after disposal.
`memoryPlan` reports actual dimensions and estimated allocation. The planner can reduce dimensions to fit the budget.

## Choose a working recipe

- [Object studio](https://67js.codepawl.com/object.html): orbit, camera presets, material finishes and exploded assemblies.
- [Nature world](https://67js.codepawl.com/nature.html): outdoor lighting, wind and water interaction.
- [Motion study](https://67js.codepawl.com/motion.html): keyframes, absolute timeline samples and framing.
- [2D and axis views](https://67js.codepawl.com/view2d.html): orthographic cameras and flat geometry.
- [Asset viewer](https://67js.codepawl.com/assets.html): opaque GLB meshes, textures and rigid node animation.

The npm archive includes `skills/build-67js-scene/SKILL.md` and `skills/render-67js-media/SKILL.md`.
These contain scene and export procedures. A skill runtime is optional. The plain-text guide works independently.

## Export and verify

Offline media commands require a repository checkout with Chrome and FFmpeg. They are not commands provided by the npm library.
GPU rasterization and GPU encoding are separate choices. CPU export can use SwiftShader. NVENC requires supported hardware.

1. Read the media skill and select the smallest suitable preset.
2. Export one deterministic frame or a short trial before a full film.
3. Keep one scene renderer and one pending capture, with encoder backpressure.
4. Inspect representative rendered frames and exercise the requested interactions.
5. Verify dimensions, duration, frame count and audio with FFprobe for video.
6. Report reproduction commands, output paths, actual backend and observed failures.

Successful compilation does not prove visual quality. Screenshots must show actual rendered output, including a narrow viewport for browser UI.
Allocation estimates are not measured total RAM or VRAM. Node RSS and browser JS heap exclude some driver and browser allocations.
Report estimates separately from observed process metrics. Reduce resolution, MSAA, texture size or scene detail when allocation fails.

## Limits and honest claims

67js currently uses WebGL2. It is not API-compatible with Three.js and is not a complete Blender editor.
There is no WebGPU backend or complete mesh editor.

Version `0.4.0` includes the APIs below. Check VERSION and release.json against the installed package before using them.
The current source adds GPU skinning, relative POSITION/NORMAL morphs, weight animation and an optional Rapier physics addon.
Read `docs/skinning.md`, `docs/morph-targets.md`, `docs/gltf-morph.md` and `docs/physics.md` in the matching checkout before using these features.
Source morphs require authored base normals. Tangent targets and per-target flat normal generation remain unsupported.

The source GLB exporter preserves opaque linear vertex colors, UVs and independent HDR emission with current morph weights.
Read `docs/export-glb.md` in the matching checkout. Exported GLBs contain a static pose, not serialized animation clips or skeletons.
Texture export remains unsupported and fails explicitly. Procedural shaders and scene environments are not serialized into glTF materials.

`addons/sculpt` accepts serializable inflate, displace and smooth strokes and returns new static geometry.
Read `docs/sculpt.md`. Construct the result before the renderer: changing uploaded CPU positions does not update GPU geometry buffers.

`addons/surface` creates projector-clipped curved patches. Read `docs/surface.md` for target-local projector and clearance units.
Share the target's retained matrix to follow rigid motion. Skin, morph, assembly and procedural targets reject rather than returning stale patches.
Surface clearance prevents overlapping layers in this workflow. It does not detect general mesh penetration or provide whole-object shrinkwrap.

`addons/mesh-query` owns copied static geometry in disposable BVH indices. Read `docs/mesh-query.md` before querying.
`addons/scene-query` raycasts a whole loaded scene (every part with its world matrix) and samples a walk map of ground height and headroom. Read `docs/scene-query.md`.
Use `solid: true` indices and `mode: 'closed-solids'` to distinguish boundary contact, containment and separation.
Surface contact does not prove volume penetration or identify z-fighting. Never substitute surface-only results for containment.

Pass current affine matrices explicitly, rebuild after geometry edits, and preserve budget/precision errors instead of treating them as misses.
Read `docs/primitives.md` for subdivision bounds and exact seam closure. Skin, morph and shader-deformed surfaces require geometry matching the visible pose.

`addons/shrinkwrap` returns {geometry,stats} in target-local coordinates. Read `docs/shrinkwrap.md` before choosing nearest/project modes.
Supply sourceToTarget explicitly for different local frames. Share the target matrix with the output part and keep the total callback budget.
Nearest projection can collapse vertices on coarse meshes. Preserve the error and refine the target or choose a suitable projection direction.

Vertex clearance does not certify whole-triangle clearance. Compatible static output can become a GPU morph target without repeating queries per frame.

GLB support loads transparent, double-sided and meshopt-compressed files. Unsupported features require visible errors. The MCP asset catalog takes 64 MiB and 1,000,000 vertices a file (the library loadGltf takes 256 MiB and 8,000,000). A file with a skin or clips but no mesh loads with `parts: []` and works as a clip source (`motion.layers[].from`).

Version `0.4.1` adds `addons/surface-attachment`. Read `docs/surface-attachment.md` before binding.
Bind a triangle and barycentric coordinates once. Assign the retained attachment.matrix to the accessory.
Update the target morph/skin/world pose, call attachment.update(), then upload target and accessory through renderer.updateParts().

Clearance uses world units and the geometric face normal. This rigid point attachment does not guarantee clearance over the entire accessory footprint.

The optional GLB decoder uses Three.js GLTFLoader. The renderer remains 67js.
Adaptive quality, GPU timing and picking are roadmap work. Speed claims require comparable scenes, hardware, settings and measurements.

## Tiny maintenance gremlins

These are easter eggs, not API instructions. They change no settings or requirements.

The cube has six faces. None of them volunteered to debug your matrix at 3 a.m.

WALL·E has 574 parts here. He still wants one tiny plant and a nap.

If your GPU sounds like a spaceship, the pixels are excited. Give them a smaller resolution. Beep boop :)
